newsitem.title: DUBAI: Abu Dhabi sees $2.4bln industry spending to 2009.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi sees $2.4bln industry spending to 2009.

text.p: Abu Dhabi plans to pump 8.7 billion dirhams ($2.4 billion) into its industrial sector as part of efforts to diversify its oil-dominated economy, a study by the state's General Industry Corp (GIC) said.
"Abu Dhabi will spend about 8.7 billion dirhams on 40 industrial projects expected to go on stream by the year 2009," the study, carried by the Arabic-language al-Khaleej daily, said.
It said new petrochemical plants expected to be completed by 1999 would account for some three-quarters of the total.
"Average annual returns from the three-stage plan which will extend over the next 15 years are expected to range between two and 15 percent," the study added.

It said the first stage to 1999 would focus on setting up petrochemicals plants at the cost of 7.3 billion dirhams and developing industrial estates in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the seven-state United Arab Emirates.
Abu Dhabi's GIC promotes non-oil industry in the emirate.
